original_rationale: Owner questionnaire on tick-preventive awareness and compliance.
title: Awareness of tick-borne disease and compliance with using tick preventive products of dog owners in Hong Kong.
rationale: Owner questionnaire on tick preventive use; no dog clinical data.

original_rationale: Randomised drug-efficacy trial. Baseline anaemia and thrombocytopenia are descriptive and not a mechanistic host-response focus.
title: Efficacy, safety and tolerance of imidocarb dipropionate versus atovaquone or buparvaquone plus azithromycin used to treat sick dogs naturally infected with the Babesia microti-like piroplasm.
rationale: Randomised trial of three regimens in 59 naturally infected sick dogs with anaemia and thrombocytopenia; clinical, laboratory and PCR outcomes to 360 days, relapses in imidocarb group.

original_rationale: Azithromycin and atovaquone treatment efficacy by PCR clearance.
title: Efficacy of Azithromycin and Compounded Atovaquone for Treatment of Babesia gibsoni in Dogs.
rationale: Prospective observational treatment study of 42 PCR-positive dogs (mostly subclinical); full text describes one dog with a haemolytic crisis (PCV 29% to 14%) given emergency transfusion plus azithromycin-atovaquone, then PCR-negative; PCR clearance reported for all.

original_rationale: Sarolaner preventive efficacy trial; no pathophysiology focus.
title: Evaluation of the efficacy of sarolaner (Simparica®) in the prevention of babesiosis in dogs.
rationale: Sarolaner prevention trial; endpoint is prevention of infection.

original_rationale: The necropsy work addresses postmortem merozoite morphology and how detection and classification are affected, not lesions or disease mechanisms.
title: Microscopic and molecular analysis of Babesia canis in archived and diagnostic specimens reveal the impact of anti-parasitic treatment and postmortem changes on pathogen detection.
rationale: Morphology of B. canis in postmortem smears; imidocarb timing relative to parasite disappearance but no clinical presentation of treated dogs.

original_rationale: Lotilaner preventive efficacy trials.
title: Two randomized, controlled studies to assess the efficacy and safety of lotilaner (Credelio™) in preventing Dermacentor reticulatus transmission of Babesia canis to dogs.
rationale: Lotilaner tick-transmission prevention trial; rescue treatment incidental.

original_rationale: Diminazene resistance mechanism in cultured parasite; no host disease link.
title: Intracellular diminazene aceturate content and adenosine incorporation in diminazene aceturate-resistant Babesia gibsoni isolate in vitro.
rationale: In vitro diminazene resistance mechanism in cultured B. gibsoni.

original_rationale: Recombinant vaccine antigen discovery and protection trial; control-dog perfusion signs are incidental, with no mechanistic host-response data.
title: Discovery of a recombinant Babesia canis supernatant antigen that protects dogs against virulent challenge infection.
rationale: Recombinant vaccine protection trial; no treatment of clinical disease.

original_rationale: African dog genomics and malaria resistance gene; no canine babesiosis data.
title: Whole-Genome Sequencing of African Dogs Provides Insights into Adaptations against Tropical Parasites.
rationale: Dog genomics; no babesiosis patients or treatment.

original_rationale: In-vitro and mouse drug screen of 17-DMAG; no canine hosts or disease mechanism.
title: 17-DMAG inhibits the multiplication of several Babesia species and Theileria equi on in vitro cultures, and Babesia microti in mice.
journal: International journal for parasitology. Drugs and drug resistance
rationale: In vitro and mouse drug screen.

original_rationale: Review of antiprotozoal drugs and drug combinations; therapeutic focus, not pathophysiology.
title: Antiprotozoal treatment of canine babesiosis.
species: B. canis, B. rossi, B. vogeli, B. gibsoni, B. conradae, B. vulpes
rationale: Review of antiprotozoal treatment of canine babesiosis, including relapse and carrier state.

original_rationale: Trends in babesiosis treatment rates from clinic records; epidemiological.
title: Canine babesiosis treatment rates in South African veterinary clinics between 2011 and 2016.
rationale: Counts of babesiosis treatments in clinic records; no clinical presentation or outcome.

original_rationale: Prevalence of cytb atovaquone-resistance mutations in diagnostic samples; no host disease mechanism.
title: Babesia gibsoni cytochrome b mutations in canine blood samples submitted to a US veterinary diagnostic laboratory.
rationale: Prevalence of cytb mutations in B. gibsoni samples; no treatment or outcome described.

original_rationale: In-vitro drug inhibition screen of phytohormone inhibitors.
title: Inhibitory effects of the phytohormone inhibitors fluridone and inabenfide against Babesia gibsoni in vitro.
rationale: In vitro screen of phytohormone inhibitors.

original_rationale: Afoxolaner efficacy in preventing B. rossi transmission by ticks.
title: Prevention of the transmission of Babesia rossi by Haemaphysalis elliptica in dogs treated with Nexgard®.
rationale: Afoxolaner prevention of B. rossi transmission.

original_rationale: Seresto collar efficacy against tick transmission; prevention trial.
title: A study on the long-term efficacy of Seresto® collars in preventing Babesia canis (Piana & Galli-Valerio, 1895) transmission to dogs by infected Dermacentor reticulatus (Fabricius, 1794) ticks.
rationale: Seresto collar prevention trial.

original_rationale: Plant extract in-vitro/mouse drug screen against bovine/equine piroplasms.
title: Inhibitory effects of Syzygium aromaticum and Camellia sinensis methanolic extracts on the growth of Babesia and Theileria parasites.
rationale: Plant extracts against bovine/equine piroplasms in vitro and mice.

original_rationale: In-vitro plant extract antibabesial screen; no host disease mechanism.
title: In vitro antioxidant and antibabesial activities of the extracts of Achillea millefolium.
rationale: In vitro plant extract screen against B. canis.

original_rationale: Drug adverse-effect case report (pancreatitis from Malarone); not babesiosis pathophysiology.
title: Malarone® induced pancreatitis and alopecia in a dog: a case report.
species: B. gibsoni (suspected; PCR negative at referral)
rationale: One dog treated with atovaquone-proguanil for suspected B. gibsoni who developed drug-induced pancreatitis and alopecia; adverse-effect report, babesiosis presentation itself not described (low confidence include).

original_rationale: In-vitro and mouse drug efficacy of hydroxyurea and eflornithine against non-canine Babesia/Theileria.
title: Safety and efficacy of hydroxyurea and eflornithine against most blood parasites Babesia and Theileria.
rationale: In vitro and mouse drug study.

original_rationale: Fluorescence-based in-vitro drug screening assay for B. gibsoni.
title: Closing the empty anti-Babesia gibsoni drug pipeline in vitro using fluorescence-based high throughput screening assay.
rationale: In vitro high-throughput drug screen.

original_rationale: In-vitro essential oil inhibition screen.
title: Inhibitory activities of essential oils against Babesia canis.
rationale: In vitro essential oil screen.

original_rationale: Experimental Ehrlichia recrudescence study; B. vogeli co-infection is incidental, pre-treated, and not analysed as a disease mechanism.
title: Ehrlichia canis in dogs experimentally infected, treated, and then immune suppressed during the acute or subclinical phases.
rationale: Experimental E. canis recrudescence study; B. vogeli/A. platys incidental and pre-treated with imidocarb.

original_rationale: Historical taxonomy and vector review. It mentions host response and cross-stock immunity only in passing and does not address pathogenesis.
title: Don't let sleeping dogs lie: unravelling the identity and taxonomy of Babesia canis, Babesia rossi and Babesia vogeli.
rationale: Historical taxonomy review; no treatment content.

original_rationale: In-vitro screen of alkaloids as antibabesial compounds.
title: Naphthylisoquinoline alkaloids and their synthetic analogs as potent novel inhibitors against Babesia canis in vitro.
rationale: In vitro alkaloid screen.

original_rationale: Retrospective antibiotic combination therapy outcomes.
title: An alternative combination therapy with metronidazole, clindamycin and doxycycline for Babesia gibsoni (Asian genotype) in dogs in Hong Kong.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Retrospective review of 24 dogs failing atovaquone/azithromycin then given triple antibiotic therapy, with PCR clearance rates; clinical syndrome only implicit.

original_rationale: Male infertility retrospective; babesiosis only a history in three dogs, no mechanistic data.
title: Clinical and spermatological findings in male dogs with acquired infertility: A retrospective analysis.
rationale: Male infertility series; babesiosis a history item in three dogs.

original_rationale: Epidemiological survey of atovaquone-resistance SNP prevalence; drug resistance, no host disease mechanism.
title: Further epidemiological survey for atovaquone resistant related gene of Babesia gibsoni in Japan during 2015-2018.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Prevalence of atovaquone-resistance SNP in B. gibsoni samples; no treated dogs described.

original_rationale: First-detection case report. Anaemia and azotaemia in B. vulpes are already recognised and the report adds no new syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: A case of Babesia vulpes infection in a dog in Russia.
journal: Veterinary parasitology, regional studies and reports
rationale: One dog with severe anaemia and azotaemia treated with imidocarb and atovaquone/azithromycin, euthanised after one week.

original_rationale: In-vitro/mouse drug combination screen.
title: Impact of using pyronaridine tetraphosphate- based combination therapy in the treatment of babesiosis caused by Babesia bovis, B. caballi, and B. gibsoni in vitro and B. microti in mice.
rationale: In vitro and mouse combination therapy study.

original_rationale: qPCR method to assess in-vitro drug inhibition.
title: Evaluation of the inhibitory effects of drugs on the growth of Babesia gibsoni using relative quantification real-time PCR.
rationale: In vitro qPCR drug inhibition method.

original_rationale: Laboratory filter method for purifying infected erythrocytes; mostly malaria models.
title: Purification of Plasmodium and Babesia- infected erythrocytes using a non-woven fabric filter.
rationale: Laboratory filter method for infected erythrocytes.

original_rationale: Recombinant vaccinia vaccine candidate immunogenicity in mice.
title: Construction of a recombinant vaccinia virus expressing Babesia gibsoni thrombospondin-related anonymous protein and evaluation of its immunogenicity in mice.
rationale: Vaccine candidate in mice.

original_rationale: HSP90 expression in diminazene-resistant isolate; parasite drug-resistance biology, no host disease link.
title: Reduced expression levels of heat shock protein 90 in a diminazene aceturate-resistant Babesia gibsoni isolate.
rationale: In vitro drug-resistant isolate HSP90 expression.

original_rationale: Prevalence and genotyping survey. The cytb mutations relate to atovaquone resistance in one relapsing dog, not to disease mechanism.
title: Babesia gibsoni emerging with high prevalence and co-infections in "fighting dogs" in Hungary.
journal: Current research in parasitology & vector-borne diseases
rationale: Prevalence and genotyping survey; one relapsing anaemic dog after atovaquone mentioned only in passing.

original_rationale: In-vitro anti-babesial activity of yarrow essential oil; drug screen.
title: Anti-babesial potential and chemical composition of essential oil from yarrow Achillea millefolium.
rationale: In vitro essential oil activity.

original_rationale: Routine case report focused on molecular identification of novel Babesia in three dogs; no pathophysiological observation.
title: Three cases of canine babesiosis caused by Babesia odocoilei-like parasites in Japan.
rationale: Three canine cases with molecular identification; abstract describes no treatment or outcome.

original_rationale: Drug efficacy study; the dog clinicopathology monitors drug side effects, and the oxidative mechanism is drug action on the parasite, not host pathophysiology.
title: Tafenoquine Is a Promising Drug Candidate for the Treatment of Babesiosis.
rationale: Tafenoquine given to B. gibsoni-infected splenectomised dogs with parasitaemia, survival, CBC and chemistry monitored (hyperkalaemia noted); mouse and in vitro work accompanies it.

original_rationale: In-vitro drug screen of natural products against B. gibsoni.
title: In vitro screening of novel anti-Babesia gibsoni drugs from natural products.
rationale: In vitro natural product screen.

original_rationale: Occurrence report with treatment response; clinical signs are listed only in general terms, with no mechanism or severity analysis.
title: Emergence of Babesia conradae infection in coyote-hunting Greyhounds in Oklahoma, USA.
rationale: 15 PCR-positive Greyhounds; ill dogs with anorexia, vomiting, fever and anaemia treated with atovaquone/azithromycin, all recovered with negative PCR at 30 and 60 days.

original_rationale: Routine case report; first molecular detection in Iran, no mechanistic content.
title: Molecular identification of Babesia canis canis genotype A in a dog from Iran.
rationale: Single dog with fever, pallor and vomiting, but no treatment or outcome is described.

original_rationale: Routine case report about diagnosis and treatment failure; it describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Co-infection with Babesia canis and Babesia gibsoni in a dog.
rationale: Dog with lethargy and anaemia; repeated treatment failures and relapse, eventual PCR clearance after metronidazole/clindamycin/doxycycline. Mixed B. canis/B. gibsoni infection.

original_rationale: First regional case report with routine clinicopathological findings; it describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
rationale: No title, journal, DOI or abstract; only the earlier rationale says it is a regional case report with clinicopathological findings, so treatment and outcome cannot be judged.

original_rationale: Routine single case with typical haemolytic presentation and azotaemia; it describes no novel complication or mechanistic investigation.
title: Babesia canis caused clinical babesiosis in a female Shih Tzu dog.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
rationale: Shih Tzu with regenerative anaemia, thrombocytopenia and azotaemia treated with diminazene and others; improved in 4 days, no recurrence at 2 months.

original_rationale: Field trial of acaricidal collar vs fipronil for tick-borne pathogen prevention; chemoprophylaxis efficacy, no disease mechanism.
title: Field trial investigating the efficacy of a long-acting imidacloprid 10%/flumethrin 4.5% polymer matrix collar (Seresto®, Elanco) compared to monthly topical fipronil for the chemoprevention of canine tick-borne pathogens in Cambodia.
journal: Current research in parasitology & vector-borne diseases
rationale: Collar versus fipronil chemoprevention field trial; endpoint is infection prevention.

original_rationale: First-detection case report of an atypical species; the clinical description is routine, with no mechanistic observation.
title: An atypical case of Babesia bigemina parasitising a dog from a rural area of eastern Mexico.
journal: Revista brasileira de parasitologia veterinaria = Brazilian journal of veterinary parasitology : Orgao Oficial do Colegio Brasileiro de Parasitologia Veterinaria
rationale: Dog with lethargy, fever, pallor and haematuria treated with imidocarb; signs reduced by day 7 and PCR negative day 30.

original_rationale: Drug screen of naphthoquine phosphate in vitro and in mice; treatment efficacy only.
title: Inhibitory effect of naphthoquine phosphate on Babesia gibsoni in vitro and Babesia rodhaini in vivo.
species: B. gibsoni in vitro; B. rodhaini mice
rationale: In vitro and mouse study; no treated dogs.

original_rationale: Drug combination efficacy and safety trial; haematology/biochemistry used only as treatment-response endpoints, not a host-mechanism focus.
title: Clinical Efficacy and Safety of Malarone®, Azithromycin and Artesunate Combination for Treatment of Babesia gibsoni in Naturally Infected Dogs.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
rationale: Twelve naturally infected dogs given Malarone, azithromycin and artesunate; haematology normalised and no relapse to 720 days.

original_rationale: Routine first-detection case report; IMHA was only a referral suspicion, with no immune-mediated mechanistic data described.
title: Babesia vulpes in a dog from Prince Edward Island, Canada.
journal: The Canadian veterinary journal = La revue veterinaire canadienne
rationale: Dog referred with suspected IMHA, confirmed B. vulpes, successfully treated with atovaquone/proguanil and azithromycin.

original_rationale: Routine co-infection case report with nonspecific signs; no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Concurrent Trypanosomosis, Babesiosis and Toxocarosis in a Dog: a Case Report.
rationale: Full text: 6-month-old dog with pale, jaundiced mucosae and emaciation, Trypanosoma, Babesia and Toxocara co-infection, treated with diminazene, doxycycline and supportive drugs; did not respond and died 20 days after presentation.

original_rationale: In vitro and in vivo drug efficacy of natural products.
title: EVALUATION OF THE INHIBITORY EFFECTS OF SIX NATURAL PRODUCT EXTRACTS AGAINST BABESIA GIBSONI IN VITRO AND IN VIVO.
rationale: Infected dogs treated with catechin or diminazene with parasite inhibition, but no clinical presentation of the dogs is described; mainly in vitro.

original_rationale: Review of splenic ultrasound terminology across many conditions in dogs and cats; Babesia is mentioned only in passing, not babesiosis pathophysiology.
title: Splenic diffuse heterogeneous hypoechogenicity pattern of dogs and cats: A systematic review.
rationale: Systematic review of splenic ultrasound pattern; no treatment.

original_rationale: Antimalarial drug efficacy mainly in mouse models; drug target focus.
title: Efficacy of the Antimalarial MMV390048 against Babesia Infection Reveals Phosphatidylinositol 4-Kinase as a Druggable Target for Babesiosis.
rationale: In vitro and mouse drug study.

original_rationale: Atovaquone/proguanil effect on parasite mitochondrial potential; drug mechanism, no host disease link.
title: The effect of atovaquone on the mitochondrial membrane potential of Babesiagibsoni.
rationale: In vitro mitochondrial potential study.

original_rationale: Drug-resistance mutations after buparvaquone-azithromycin; the haematology data are minor treatment-response endpoints.
title: Multiple point mutations in cytochrome b gene of Babesia gibsoni - A possible cause for buparvaquone resistance.
rationale: Twelve dogs given buparvaquone-azithromycin; haematology improved, 8 had persistent parasitaemia and were genotyped for cytb mutations. Clinical syndrome only lightly described.

original_rationale: Routine first-record case report of B. canis in a new region; no mechanistic observation.
title: The First Records of Canine Babesiosis in Dogs from Dermacentor reticulatus-Free Zone in Poland.
rationale: Two symptomatic cases reported for geographic novelty; no treatment or outcome in the abstract.

original_rationale: Haematological alterations pooled across multiple vector-borne infections, mostly Ehrlichia; no Babesia-specific analysis.
title: Haematological Alterations Associated with Selected Vector-Borne Infections and Exposure in Dogs from Pereira, Risaralda, Colombia.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
rationale: Haematological survey of vector-borne infections; no treatment.

original_rationale: Leishmaniosis comorbidity study; Babesia seropositivity is only a risk factor for CanL, with no babesiosis pathophysiology.
title: Investigation of comorbidities in dogs with leishmaniosis due to Leishmania infantum.
journal: Veterinary parasitology, regional studies and reports
rationale: Leishmaniosis comorbidity study; Babesia is a seroprevalence risk factor only.

original_rationale: Preprint, so excluded by the peer-review rule; it is also mainly a supportive-treatment efficacy study.
title: Therapeutic efficacy of Oral Carica papaya leaf juice extract in the supportive care of infectious thrombocytopenia in bleeding dogs.
rationale: Preprint, so excluded under the peer-review rule.

original_rationale: Multi-species review of Pakistani status, distribution and chemotherapy; the generic clinical-sign list does not address canine pathogenesis.
title: Babesiosis: Current status and future perspectives in Pakistan and chemotherapy used in livestock and pet animals.
rationale: Multi-species review covering clinical signs and chemotherapy of babesiosis in pet animals including dogs; canine content is generic, so borderline.

original_rationale: In vitro drug screen of FDA-approved compounds.
title: In vitro screening of compounds from the Food and Drug Administration-approved library identifies anti-Babesia gibsoni activity of idarubicin hydrochloride and vorinostat.
rationale: In vitro drug screen.

original_rationale: Stakeholder disease-prioritisation for UK surveillance; no pathophysiology.
title: Stakeholder opinion-led study to identify canine priority diseases for surveillance and control in the UK.
rationale: Stakeholder prioritisation study; no dog data.

original_rationale: Field efficacy trial of fluralaner for preventing transmission.
title: Field efficacy of fluralaner (Bravecto® chewable tablets) for preventing Babesia canis infection transmitted by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks to dogs.
rationale: Fluralaner transmission prevention field trial in healthy dogs.

original_rationale: In-vitro/mouse anti-babesial compound screen.
title: Anti-babesial activity of a series of 6,7-dimethoxyquinazoline-2,4-diamines (DMQDAs).
rationale: In vitro and mouse compound screen.

original_rationale: Genetic diversity and atovaquone-resistance marker survey of isolates; epidemiological genotyping with no host disease link.
title: Analysis of Genetic Diversity of cytb gene from Babesia gibsoni Isolates from Naturally Infected Dogs in Karnataka, India.
rationale: Cytb genetic diversity survey; no treated dogs described.

original_rationale: Qualitative interviews on outbreak notification thresholds; surveillance methodology.
title: Setting clinically relevant thresholds for the notification of canine disease outbreaks to veterinary practitioners: an exploratory qualitative interview study.
rationale: Qualitative interview study on outbreak thresholds.

original_rationale: Romiplostim efficacy study in thrombocytopenia of mixed causes. Only one babesiosis dog, so no babesiosis pathophysiology.
title: Romiplostim for treatment of thrombocytopenia in dogs: A retrospective assessment and clinical outcomes.
rationale: Romiplostim in thrombocytopenia of mixed causes; a single dog had babesiosis.

original_rationale: Case report on imidocarb failure and suspected resistance. Relapsing pancytopenia is a routine course, not a distinct syndrome or mechanism.
title: Repeated imidocarb treatment failure suggesting emerging resistance of Babesia canis in a new endemic area in north-eastern Germany.
rationale: Dog with repeated relapses and pancytopenia after multiple imidocarb doses; resolved with atovaquone/azithromycin.

original_rationale: Acaricide transmission-prevention trial. Placebo dogs are reported only as showing clinical signs, with no pathophysiological data.
title: Evaluation of the efficacy of Simparica Trio® in the prevention of the transmission of Babesia canis by infected Dermacentor reticulatus to dogs.
rationale: Experimental transmission prevention trial with a combination acaricide.

original_rationale: Melioidosis seroprevalence study. The platelet finding concerns melioidosis plus pooled blood-pathogen co-infection, not babesiosis.
title: Seroprevalence of melioidosis and its association with blood profiles and pathogens in sheltered dogs in southern Thailand.
rationale: Melioidosis seroprevalence study; no treatment.

original_rationale: Veterinarian knowledge-attitude-practice survey.
title: Knowledge, attitude, and practices of veterinarians towards canine vector-borne pathogens in Sri Lanka.
rationale: Veterinarian knowledge-attitude-practice survey; no dog-level clinical data.

original_rationale: Case report focused on transmammary treatment and vertical transmission. A single puppy death gives no pathophysiological insight.
title: Successful Transmammary Treatment of Babesia gibsoni Infection in Newborn Puppies after the Administration of Malarone®, Azithromycin, and Artesunate to a Lactating Dam.
rationale: Infected dam and puppy litter treated via lactating dam, with PCR clearance and one puppy death. Clinical presentation is thin but outcome is clear.

original_rationale: qPCR standardization used to compare parasitaemia between treatment regimens. Diagnostic and treatment focus, with no host pathophysiology.
title: Standardization of quantitative PCR (qPCR) method to detect the level of parasitaemia in Babesia gibsoni infected dogs.
rationale: Two-arm treatment comparison in dogs diagnosed with babesiosis (clinical cases), with qPCR parasitaemia before and on day 10 of treatment; meets the trial rule of thumb although signs are not listed.

original_rationale: In vitro and mouse drug efficacy study of sitamaquine.
title: Evaluation of the inhibitory effects of sitamaquine on Babesia infections.
rationale: In vitro and mouse drug study.

original_rationale: Chemical analysis of artemisinin supplement capsule strength; no host data.
title: Analysis of US Marketed Artemisinin Supplements for Use in Dogs.
journal: Journal of veterinary pharmacology and therapeutics
rationale: Chemical analysis of artemisinin supplement capsules; no dogs.

original_rationale: Routine diagnostic case report of a fatal co-infection. No distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, and E. canis confounds the findings.
title: Concurrent infection of Babesia canis vogeli and Ehrlichia canis in a non-descriptive Indian dog: case study.
journal: Journal of parasitic diseases : official organ of the Indian Society for Parasitology
rationale: Two-month-old pup with severe anaemia, thrombocytopenia and hepatic changes, co-infected with E. canis; treated but died the same day.

original_rationale: Doxycycline efficacy trial in triple infection. Haematological recovery is a treatment outcome, and Babesia effects cannot be separated from the other pathogens.
title: Improvements in Blood Profiles of Canines Naturally Infected with Triple Blood Pathogens (Babesia vogeli, Ehrlichia canis, and Anaplasma platys) Subsequent to Doxycycline Monotherapy.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
rationale: Thirty-four dogs with B. vogeli, E. canis and A. platys given doxycycline; PCR clearance and blood profile recovery.

original_rationale: Parasite gene expression under diminazene in culture; drug resistance, no host disease link.
title: Analysis of gene expression of Babesia gibsoni cultured with diminazene aceturate using RNA sequencing.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Parasite gene expression in culture.

original_rationale: Clinic register of disease frequencies and mortality. Babesiosis is one listed category, with no clinical or mechanistic data.
title: Prevalence of common conditions and associated mortalities of dogs treated at the small animal clinic, Makerere University, Kampala, Uganda.
rationale: Clinic register of disease frequency and mortality; no case-level treatment data.

original_rationale: First-detection case report. Haemolytic anaemia and thrombocytopenia are the expected presentation, with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Case report: First autochthonous Babesia vulpes infection in a dog from Italy.
rationale: Dog with severe haemolytic anaemia and thrombocytopenia; imidocarb partly effective, resolved with Malarone and azithromycin.

original_rationale: N-acetylcysteine therapy study using a cyclophosphamide rat model. Canine data are treatment responses in mixed hemoprotozoan cases.
title: N-acetylcysteine enhances bone marrow activity in treating pancytopenia induced by canine hemoprotozoan diseases.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
rationale: Clinical dogs with pancytopenia from babesiosis/ehrlichiosis given NAC plus specific therapy, with haematological response; rat model is supplementary.

original_rationale: Household One Health outbreak report, mostly about humans and Bartonella. Canine pathology is not linked to Babesia mechanistically.
title: A One Health Zoonotic Vector Borne Infectious Disease Family Outbreak Investigation.
rationale: One dog was Babesia-positive in a household outbreak study; no babesia syndrome or treatment of the dog is described.

original_rationale: Tafenoquine efficacy study. Hct, platelet and relapse data are treatment-response endpoints, not pathophysiology.
title: Efficacy of tafenoquine in dogs naturally infected with Babesia gibsoni.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Eight naturally infected dogs given tafenoquine; clinical improvement, Hct/platelets and two relapses reported.

original_rationale: Acaricide transmission-prevention trial. Control dogs' clinical signs served only as an infection endpoint, with no host-response data.
title: Efficacy of an oral combination of afoxolaner and milbemycin oxime for the prevention of transmission of Babesia canis by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks to dogs.
rationale: Transmission-prevention acaricide trial; control dogs rescue-treated but no treatment response reported.

original_rationale: Antibabesial drug efficacy and resistance mutations; no host disease mechanism.
title: Efficacy and mechanism of action of cipargamin as an antibabesial drug candidate.
species: B. bovis, B. gibsoni in vitro, B. microti mice
rationale: In vitro and mouse study of cipargamin; no treated dogs.

original_rationale: Routine coinfection case report with smear-only Babesia identification. No distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Case report of a triple vector-borne infection in a dog: co-infection with Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Babesia spp., and Dirofilaria repens in North-Eastern Poland.
rationale: Dog with triple co-infection, fever and thrombocytopenia; treated with complete improvement by day 2.

original_rationale: Drug-resistance mutation prevalence and treatment response (n=9). This is resistance genotyping, not virulence or host pathophysiology.
title: Pyrosequencing analysis of cytochrome b (CYTb) gene mutations in Babesia gibsoni: Correlation with drug resistance and treatment efficacy in South Korea.
journal: Veterinary parasitology, regional studies and reports
rationale: Reports regimens used and treatment response by CYTb mutation status in nine dogs; borderline since the focus is genotyping.

original_rationale: Routine single-case report with regional molecular characterisation and therapy. Uncontrolled oxidant data do not make it a distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Molecular characterization, phylogenetic analysis, and successful therapeutic management of Babesia gibsoni infection in a 1.5-year-old female spitz from Tripura.
journal: Journal of parasitic diseases : official organ of the Indian Society for Parasitology
rationale: Spitz with anaemia and haemoglobinuria treated with triple therapy; recovered by day 10.

original_rationale: Preprint, so it fails the peer-review criterion. It is also mainly a therapeutic-failure case report.
title: Therapeutic Failure and Relapse of Babesia gibsoni Infection in a Working Dog
rationale: Preprint of a treatment failure and relapse case; excluded as not peer reviewed.

original_rationale: Persistent haemolysis caused by inherited PKLR deficiency, with Babesia excluded as the cause. Not babesiosis pathophysiology.
title: From Mutation to Manifestation: Evaluation of a PKLR Gene Truncation Caused by Exon Skipping in a Schnauzer Terrier.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
rationale: Persistent anaemia was due to inherited PKLR deficiency; Babesia was an initial infection and not the focus.

original_rationale: Multi-species sialic acid biomarker review. Canine babesiosis is a minor mention, not a review of its pathogenesis.
title: Serum Sialic Acid as a Biomarker of Inflammation and Infection: Insights From Veterinary Medicine.
rationale: Multi-species sialic acid biomarker review without canine babesiosis treatment.

original_rationale: Single case focused on imidocarb dosing failure; routine haematology and anecdotal corticosteroid comment, no distinct syndrome or mechanistic data.
title: Treatment failure in a dog with acute Babesia canis infection using lower-range therapeutic doses of imidocarb dipropionate.
rationale: Dog with imidocarb treatment failure at low doses, resolved after higher doses.

original_rationale: Drug regimen comparison; baseline haemato-biochemical abnormalities are descriptive outcome measures, not the mechanistic focus.
title: Comparative therapeutic efficacy of Artesunate-Atovaquone-Azithromycin and Doxycycline-Clindamycin-Metronidazole regimens in dogs naturally infected with Babesia gibsoni.
