journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
rationale: Molecular identification of two cases; signs only called consistent with babesiosis and no treatment is given.

original_rationale: Based on abstract: a single puppy with triple co-infection, so the anaemia, thrombocytopenia and hypergammaglobulinaemia cannot be attributed to Babesia, and no distinct Babesia syndrome or mechanism is described.
title: Triplice infezione da Ehrlichia spp., Babesia spp. ed Hepatozoon spp. in un cucciolo
journal: CINECA IRIS Institutional Research Information System (University of Bari Aldo Moro)
rationale: Puppy with triple co-infection; findings described but no treatment or outcome in the abstract.

original_rationale: Based on Springer landing-page abstract: single fatal dog with concurrent babesiosis and ehrlichiosis (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, seizures); the neurological signs are attributed to the co-infection, so Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated.
title: A complicated case of concurrent canine babesiosis and canine ehrlichiosis
rationale: Single dog with concurrent babesiosis and ehrlichiosis, anaemia, thrombocytopenia and seizures, which died (per earlier landing-page reading); whether treatment was given before death is not confirmed.

original_rationale: Based on abstract: a routine single case of diagnosis, molecular confirmation and treatment; the anaemia and thrombocytopenia are only noted, and the criteria exclude routine case reports with no distinct syndrome or mechanism.
title: Molecular characterisation of Babesia gibsoni infection from a pit-bull terrier pup recently imported into South Africa.
journal: Journal of the South African Veterinary Association
rationale: Pup with anaemia and thrombocytopenia failed diminazene and imidocarb (PCR still positive) then cleared with atovaquone plus azithromycin.

original_rationale: Review of vaccine development using soluble parasite antigens. It covers vaccine protection and not host pathophysiology of disease.
title: Vaccination against large Babesia species from dogs.
rationale: Review of vaccine development with no treatment of clinical disease.

original_rationale: Routine co-infection case report of an imported dog. Babesia was not confirmed by PCR and there are no separable host pathophysiological data.
title: Molecular and serological evidence for Anaplasma platys and Babesia sp. infection in a dog, imported in Belgium, from Southern Spain.
journal: Journal of veterinary medicine. A, Physiology, pathology, clinical medicine
rationale: Import case of Anaplasma platys and Babesia co-infection; no treatment or outcome in the abstract.

original_rationale: Based on abstract: fatal case in a 6-week-old pup with six concurrent pathogens; the thrombocytopenia, anaemia and hypoproteinaemia are attributed to the multi-pathogen infection, so Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated.
title: Coinfection with multiple tick-borne and intestinal parasites in a 6-week-old dog.
journal: The Canadian veterinary journal = La revue veterinaire canadienne
rationale: Fatal multi-pathogen infection in a 6-week-old pup; no treatment is described.

original_rationale: In vitro screening of plant extracts for antibabesial activity and natural-product chemistry. No host data.
title: Screening of Indonesian medicinal plant extracts for antibabesial activity and isolation of new quassinoids from Brucea javanica.
rationale: In vitro plant extract screening with no dogs.

original_rationale: National veterinary drug adverse-reaction report; the piroplasmosis vaccine reactions are in vaccinated dogs, not infected dogs. No pathophysiological data.
title: [Reported adverse reactions due to veterinary drugs in 2006].
rationale: National adverse drug reaction report; piroplasmosis vaccine reactions are in vaccinated dogs.

original_rationale: Based on the title, record type (Letter) and MeSH only; the publisher page returned 403. The endpoint is remission of demodicosis after treating concurrent babesiosis and/or ehrlichiosis, with no measured Babesia-specific host pathophysiology, which matches the round-3 exclusion of a demodicosis-babesiosis report.
title: Remission of cunical signs of adult-onset generalized demodicosis after treatment for concurrent babesiosis and/or granulocytic ehrlichiosis in dogs.
rationale: Letter whose title reports remission of demodicosis after treating concurrent babesiosis and/or granulocytic ehrlichiosis; MeSH lists antiprotozoal and antibacterial agents (therapeutic use). No abstract to confirm babesiosis presentation or numbers.

original_rationale: Reference-list entry; the title describes a prevalence and seasonality study, which suggests no host pathophysiological data.
title: Prevalence and seasonality of babesiosis in dogs treated at university veterinary clinic in Kaduna Nigeria from 1990–1999, Niger
rationale: Reference-list entry for a prevalence and seasonality study; no treatment data.

original_rationale: Based on the reconstructed abstract: a short German practitioner-magazine update covering vectors and transmission routes, with no pathophysiology focus. This is consistent with the earlier exclusion of practitioner updates.
title: Babesiose/Piroplasmose – ein Update
rationale: Practitioner update on vectors and transmission; no treatment or clinical data in the abstract.

original_rationale: Canis lupus counts as canine, but this is a routine single case (depression, haematuria, antibiotic treatment) with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: The case of babesiosis in farmed wolf (Canis lupus L).
rationale: Farmed wolf with typical signs treated with antibiotics with a positive result. Brief, but both parts are present.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: this is a single pup with B. canis, B. gibsoni and E. canis triple infection, and E. canis can also cause respiratory signs, so the diffuse lung disease and anaemia cannot be attributed to Babesia. A one-dog report cannot separate Babesia-specific host data, and the report focuses on management and treatment.
title: Management of respiratory syndrome associated with a mixed infection of Babesia canis, Babesia gibsoni and Ehrlichia canis in a Great Dane Pup
rationale: Pup with mixed Babesia and E. canis infection, respiratory signs and anaemia, treated with babesicidals, antirickettsials and supportive therapy; uneventful recovery.

original_rationale: Title only: OpenAlex has no abstract (Indian Vet J 85(10):1037-1039). This is a short comparative drug-efficacy note, and earlier rounds excluded title-only drug comparisons such as imidocarb vs diminazene as treatment_efficacy. Nothing indicates mechanistic or host-pathophysiology outcomes.
title: COMPARATIVE EFFICACY OF CLINDAMYCIN VIS-A-VIS DIMINAZINE ACETURATE IN CANINE BABESIOSIS
rationale: Title indicates a comparison of clindamycin and diminazene in canine babesiosis (Indian Vet J 85(10):1037-1039); no abstract to confirm clinical status or outcomes.

original_rationale: In vitro drug growth-inhibition screen with no host data.
title: In vitro evaluation of the growth inhibitory activities of 15 drugs against Babesia gibsoni (Aomori strain).
rationale: In vitro drug growth-inhibition screen with no dogs.

original_rationale: Based on the title only; the Wiley landing page returned 403 and no abstract is available. The title describes a routine single imported travel case in a CPD journal and points to no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Medicine: Babesiosis in a 10-year-old British crossbreed dog returning from vacation in France
rationale: Title describes a single imported case in a CPD journal; no abstract, so signs, treatment and outcome are unknown.

original_rationale: Based on the title and OpenAlex metadata only (abstract not reachable): a one-page case report (Indian J Field Vet 4(4):65, 2009) with a generic title. This points to a routine single case of diagnosis and treatment, with no distinct syndrome named.
title: Babesiosis in a dog - a case report.
rationale: One-page case report with a generic title; no abstract to show presentation, treatment or outcome.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract; the full-text PDF from the publisher returned no content. This is a pharmacology study of imidocarb-induced cholinesterase inhibition, with atropine pretreatment. Babesia appears only as the drug's indication, and nothing indicates infected dogs or host data on babesiosis.
title: Effects of imidocarb on cholinesterase activity and grossly observable behaviour in dogs.
rationale: Imidocarb cholinesterase inhibition and toxicity study in non-infected dogs.

original_rationale: Study of neutrophil left shift and toxic change in extreme leukocytosis from many causes. Babesiosis is mentioned only in passing, with no Babesia-specific data.
title: Neutrophilic left shift and toxic change in canine extreme granulocytic leukocytosis cases
rationale: Neutrophil left shift in extreme leukocytosis of mixed causes; babesiosis only a listed cause and no treatment.

original_rationale: Based on the title and PubMed metadata (no abstract; the Vet Rec landing page was blocked). This is a 2-page single-dog report of an atypical presentation (ascites) with a triple co-infection, so Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated as the mixed-infection rule requires.
title: Atypical clinical presentation of coinfection with Ehrlichia, Babesia and Hepatozoon species in a dog.
rationale: Single dog with Ehrlichia, Babesia and Hepatozoon co-infection presenting with ascites; no abstract and no therapeutic-use MeSH terms, so treatment and outcome are unknown.

original_rationale: The title shows a hospital prevalence and seasonality study from 1990-1999. No abstract, but the title points clearly to epidemiology only.
title: Prevalence and seasonality of babesiosis in dogs treated at a univerisity veterinary clinic in Kaduna, Nigeria from 1990-1999
rationale: Hospital prevalence and seasonality study; epidemiological only.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a DNA/vaccinia prime-boost vaccine trial. The endpoints are vaccine-induced IgG2, IFN-gamma and lower parasitaemia after challenge, which measure vaccine efficacy rather than the mechanisms of disease. This matches the rounds 1-3 precedent (PMID:29279083), where a vaccine protection trial with only incidental host-response data was excluded as treatment_efficacy.
title: Immunogenicity and growth inhibitory efficacy of the prime-boost immunization regime with DNA followed by recombinant vaccinia virus carrying the P29 gene of Babesia gibsoni in dogs.
rationale: DNA and vaccinia prime-boost vaccine trial with challenge; endpoints are immune response and parasitaemia, no treatment of disease.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a PCR prevalence and risk-factor survey in sled dogs. The acute, asymptomatic and under-treatment groups are clinical status labels only, and no haematological, biochemical or other host markers are reported.
title: Babesia canis and other tick-borne infections in dogs in Central Poland.
rationale: PCR prevalence survey in sled dogs; three dogs were 'undergoing treatment' but no signs, therapy or outcome are described.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a single case of an incidental infection found on a blood smear in a dog with lymphoma, with persistent PCR positivity after imidocarb. The authors only suggest immunocompromise as one possible cause, next to drug failure. There is no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, so this is a routine case of diagnosis and treatment.
title: Detection of a large unnamed Babesia piroplasm originally identified in dogs in North Carolina in a dog with no history of travel to that state.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
species: Babesia sp. (North Carolina large piroplasm, PCR)
rationale: One immunosuppressed lymphoma dog with incidental parasitaemia treated with imidocarb twice; PCR stayed positive to 50 weeks (treatment failure). Clinical syndrome is weak but treatment failure cases are eligible.

original_rationale: Development of a FRET-PCR with frequency and therapy monitoring; no host pathophysiological data for infected dogs.
title: Frequency and therapy monitoring of canine Babesia spp. infection by high-resolution melting curve quantitative FRET-PCR.
rationale: Diagnostic PCR paper; therapy monitoring is mentioned (atovaquone and tilmicosin cleared B. gibsoni, doxycycline and berenil did not) but no clinical presentation of the treated dogs is given.

original_rationale: Review of epidemiology, diagnosis, treatment and control of hepatozoonosis, babesiosis and cytauxzoonosis; not focused on pathophysiology or syndromes.
title: Canine hepatozoonosis and babesiosis, and feline cytauxzoonosis.
journal: The Veterinary clinics of North America. Small animal practice
rationale: Narrative review covering epidemiology, diagnosis, treatment and control of canine babesiosis.

original_rationale: Pharmacokinetics of diminazene in healthy dogs; no infected-dog host data.
title: The intravenous pharmacokinetics of diminazene in healthy dogs.
journal: Journal of the South African Veterinary Association
rationale: Intravenous pharmacokinetics of diminazene in six healthy dogs.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: an in vitro antibabesial drug study. The haemolysis, ATP depletion and Na,K-ATPase changes are caused by the ionophores in HK erythrocytes, not by infection, so it reports no pathophysiology in infected dogs.
title: Effects and mechanisms of action of ionophorous antibiotics valinomycin and salinomycin-Na on Babesia gibsoni in vitro.
rationale: In vitro culture study of ionophores on canine erythrocytes; no infected dogs.

original_rationale: Title only, checked on the OpenAlex record: no abstract (PubVet 4(2), 2010). A single case of Ehrlichia and Babesia co-infection, with no sign of a distinct syndrome and no way to separate Babesia-specific host data, is a routine case report.
title: Ehrlichiosis × babesiosis dog: a case report.
rationale: Title indicates a single Ehrlichia and Babesia co-infection case report; no abstract available.

original_rationale: Clinic note on routine diagnosis and etiological and symptomatic treatment of pet dogs; no pathophysiological content.
title: Clinical Diagnosis and Treatment of Pet Dog Babesiosis
rationale: Clinic report of pet dogs clinically diagnosed with babesiosis and given aetiological plus symptomatic treatment with good curative effect; signs, drugs and numbers are not given in the abstract, so this is a weak include.

original_rationale: Title only, checked on the OpenAlex record: a two-page note (Vet Practitioner 11(2):120-121, 2010) with no abstract. The title frames it as an imidocarb efficacy evaluation, and nothing points to mechanistic host outcomes.
title: Evaluation of imidocarb dipropionate for the treatment of canine babesiosis.
rationale: Two-page note evaluating imidocarb for canine babesiosis (Vet Practitioner 11(2):120-121); no abstract to confirm clinical status or outcome.

original_rationale: In vitro development of a diminazene-resistant B. gibsoni strain and IC50 values; no host data.
title: Development and characterization of a strain of Babesia gibsoni resistant to diminazene aceturate in vitro.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: In vitro development of a diminazene-resistant strain; no dogs.

original_rationale: Routine single case of first autochthonous B. canis canis infection in Norway, with diagnosis and imidocarb treatment and no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: First case of babesiosis caused by Babesia canis canis in a dog from Norway.
syndromes: other: clinical signs of babesiosis (not specified)
rationale: Irish setter with signs of babesiosis and B. canis canis confirmed by PCR; MeSH lists imidocarb (therapeutic use) but the abstract gives no treatment details or outcome.

original_rationale: Retrospective comparison of drug combinations with efficacy and recovery time as endpoints; no mechanistic outcomes.
title: Use of a doxycycline-enrofloxacin-metronidazole combination with/without diminazene diaceturate to treat naturally occurring canine babesiosis caused by Babesia gibsoni.
rationale: Retrospective comparison of doxycycline-enrofloxacin-metronidazole with or without diminazene in naturally infected dogs; efficacy 85.7% vs 83.3% and recovery time reported.

original_rationale: Field trial of imidacloprid/permethrin prevention with infection incidence as the endpoint; no host pathophysiological data.
title: Prevention of endemic canine vector-borne diseases using imidacloprid 10% and permethrin 50% in young dogs: a longitudinal field study.
species: Babesia spp. and other CVBD agents
rationale: Field prevention trial of imidacloprid and permethrin with infection incidence as the endpoint.

original_rationale: Artesunate in vitro and mouse efficacy study; endpoints are parasite growth inhibition, with no host pathophysiology in dogs.
title: Artesunate, a potential drug for treatment of Babesia infection.
species: B. gibsoni, B. bovis (in vitro), B. microti (mice)
rationale: In vitro and mouse study of artesunate; no infected dogs.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a single case report whose point is molecular species identification. Haemoglobinuria and fever appear only as presenting complaints, with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, and the criteria have no host-marker rule that admits routine case reports, so the rescue is not upheld.
title: Babesia canis and Babesia rossi co-infection in an untraveled Nigerian dog.
rationale: Case report of anorexia, haemoglobinuria and fever focused on species identification; no treatment or outcome in the abstract.

original_rationale: Hsp70 transcript levels in diminazene-resistant parasite variants in culture; no host data.
title: Reduced transcript levels of the heat shock protein 70 gene in diminazene aceturate-resistant Babesia gibsoni variants under low concentrations of diminazene aceturate.
journal: The Japanese journal of veterinary research
rationale: Hsp70 transcript levels in diminazene-resistant cultured parasites; no dogs.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a routine single case of icterus with hyperbilirubinaemia, diagnosed by smear and treated. Hyperbilirubinaemia is an expected finding, not a distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, so the rescue is not upheld.
title: Jaundice In Dog Associated With Babesiosis
journal: International Journal for Agro Veterinary and Medical Sciences
rationale: Labrador bitch with jaundice and hyperbilirubinaemia treated; parasites cleared by day 5 and the dog recovered by day 15.

original_rationale: Based on the full text (DOI landing PDF, Vet World 2011;4(6):269-270, online 2011-03-25): a routine single case of severe anaemia (Hb 3 g/dl, PCV 20%) diagnosed by smear and treated with diminazene, oxytetracycline and transfusion. It describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Babesia gibsoni infection in a German Shepherd dog
rationale: Earlier full-text screen recorded a German Shepherd with severe anaemia (Hb 3 g/dl, PCV 20%) treated with diminazene, oxytetracycline and transfusion; outcome was not recorded and the PDF could not be re-read. Likely include if recovery is stated.

original_rationale: From the abstract: a routine single case of haemolytic jaundice with hyperbilirubinaemia, diagnosis and recovery after treatment, which is the expected presentation, with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation. Rounds 1-3 excluded such cases the same way; the case-report rule applies, not a host-marker rescue.
title: Jaundice in dog associated with babesiosis - A case report
rationale: Labrador bitch with jaundice and hyperbilirubinaemia given antibabesial and supportive therapy; negative by day 5 and fully recovered by day 15 (likely the same case as the other jaundice record).

original_rationale: From the abstract: a routine single case of diagnosis and cure, where the paralysis comes from the tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis) and not from babesiosis. The only host finding is non-specific low haemoglobin, so it shows no distinct babesiosis syndrome or mechanism, in line with how rounds 1-3 handled routine case reports.
title: Diagnosis and Curat of Tick Paralysis and Babesia gibsoni Infection of the Tibetan Mastiff Canine Induced by Tick Invasion
rationale: Tibetan Mastiff puppy with paralysis, low haemoglobin and B. gibsoni on smear, cured after ivermectin and Xuechongjing within 3 days.

original_rationale: Case report of first molecular detection in Portugal and possible vertical transmission. It gives no host pathophysiological data.
title: Babesiosis due to the canine Babesia microti-like small piroplasm in dogs-first report from Portugal and possible vertical transmission.
rationale: Molecular first report in three dogs; no clinical signs, treatment or outcome described.

original_rationale: In vitro anti-babesial activity of nystatin. The host-cell effects measured are drug effects on normal erythrocytes, not infection pathophysiology.
title: Effects and mechanisms of action of polyene macrolide antibiotic nystatin on Babesia gibsoni in vitro.
rationale: In vitro nystatin study on cultured parasites and canine cells; no infected dogs.

original_rationale: Trial of an acaricide for blocking tick transmission. Endpoints are transmission and clinical signs, with no mechanistic host data.
title: The prevention of transmission of Babesia canis canis by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks to dogs using a novel combination of fipronil, amitraz and (S)-methoprene.
rationale: Acaricide transmission-blocking trial; endpoint is prevention of infection, with no treatment of clinical disease.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a single case report of a first US diagnosis in an imported dog, with the usual anaemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and mild azotaemia and a good response to imidocarb. One routine case does not meet the case-report threshold, which needs a distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation; rounds 1-3 excluded similar first-detection cases.
title: Babesia canis rossi infection in a Texas dog.
rationale: Imported puppy with fever, anaemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and azotaemia; responded to imidocarb and PCR was negative 2 weeks later.

original_rationale: In vitro development of atovaquone resistance and its parasite genetics. No host data.
title: Development of in vitro atovaquone-resistant Babesia gibsoni with a single-nucleotide polymorphism in cytb.
rationale: In vitro atovaquone-resistant strain with cytb SNP; no dogs.

original_rationale: Vaccine safety study in vaccinated, uninfected dogs. The local reactions, CRP and ESR are vaccine effects, not infection pathophysiology.
title: [Comparative safety study of two commercialised vaccines against canine babesiosis induced by Babesia canis].
rationale: Vaccine safety study in uninfected dogs.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a single-puppy case whose subject is the parasite looking small after death or after tissue storage. The necropsy lesions (icterus, splenomegaly, haemoglobin nephrosis) are routine and not analysed as mechanism, matching how round 1 treated the postmortem-morphology paper PMID:29047398.
title: Postmortem small babesia-like morphology of Babesia canis - short communication.
rationale: Puppy with severe anaemia and haemoglobinuria was euthanised; the paper is about post-mortem parasite morphology and describes no treatment.

original_rationale: Atovaquone with azithromycin treatment, with PCR clearance as the endpoint. It also reports re-emergence of the species but gives no host pathophysiological data.
title: Re-emergence of Babesia conradae and effective treatment of infected dogs with atovaquone and azithromycin.
rationale: Twelve naturally infected dogs, partly randomised placebo-controlled; atovaquone plus azithromycin cleared B. conradae DNA on PCR whereas placebo dogs stayed positive. Presentation is thin (haemolytic anaemia only).

original_rationale: Abstract: a single co-infected dog whose thrombocytopenia, anaemia and raised CRP cannot be attributed to B. vogeli rather than A. platys, and the report centres on the first detection of A. platys. It describes no Babesia-specific distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: First case of Anaplasma platys infection in a dog from Croatia.
rationale: A. platys first-detection case with B. vogeli co-infection; laboratory abnormalities only, no treatment or outcome.

original_rationale: Practice recommendations covering many canine vector-borne diseases, with no babesiosis pathophysiology content.
title: Vector-borne diseases--constant challenge for practicing veterinarians: recommendations from the CVBD World Forum.
rationale: CVBD World Forum practice recommendations on prevention and treatment of canine vector-borne diseases, explicitly including babesiosis; included as a guideline-type review whose subject includes treatment, though depth of babesiosis treatment coverage was not verified.

original_rationale: Abstract (OpenAlex, reconstructed): a single case report focused on diagnosing concurrent infections, with no laboratory values and no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation. With three pathogens, Babesia-specific host data could not be separated even if the full text has a haemogram.
title: DIAGNÓSTICO DE INFECÇÕES CONCOMITANTES POR Neospora caninum, Babesia canis e Erhlichia spp. EM CANINO ADULTO DA RAÇA GOLDEN RETRIVIER - RELATO DE CASO*
journal: LA Referencia (Red Federada de Repositorios Institucionales de Publicaciones Científicas)
rationale: Case report of concurrent Neospora, Babesia and Ehrlichia infection centred on diagnosis; the abstract describes no treatment or outcome.

original_rationale: Abstract: the syndrome is tick paralysis attributed to R. sanguineus toxin, not babesiosis. Only 2 of 14 dogs had B. vogeli, mixed with H. canis, and the haematology is not reported by parasite, so there are no separable Babesia-specific host data.
title: Apparent tick paralysis by Rhipicephalus sanguineus (Acari: Ixodidae) in dogs.
rationale: Dogs treated for tick paralysis by R. sanguineus; Babesia was found in only two and was not the treated condition.

original_rationale: Mitochondrial genes and diminazene resistance in cultured B. gibsoni, with no host data.
title: Involvement of mitochondrial genes of Babesia gibsoni in resistance to diminazene aceturate.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Mitochondrial genes of a diminazene-resistant cultured isolate; no dogs.

original_rationale: Survey of the parasite cytochrome b gene for atovaquone-resistance mutations in 92 samples, with no host data.
title: Molecular epidemiological survey of the Babesia gibsoni cytochrome b gene in western Japan.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Parasite cytb genotyping survey for atovaquone-resistance mutations; no treated dogs described.

original_rationale: Vaccine safety study in uninfected dogs. The haematology and biochemistry are vaccine reactions, not host data from infected dogs.
title: Preliminary Study on the Safety of a New Vaccine Against Canine Babesiosis Containing Soluble Parasitic Antigen (SPA)
rationale: Safety study of a candidate vaccine in uninfected dogs.

original_rationale: In vitro energy and glycolysis metabolism of diminazene-resistant B. gibsoni isolates; parasite-side data only.
title: Analysis of energy generation and glycolysis pathway in diminazene aceturate-resistant Babesia gibsoni isolate in vitro.
journal: The Japanese journal of veterinary research
rationale: In vitro energy metabolism of a diminazene-resistant isolate; no dogs.

original_rationale: Duplicate record of DOI:10.3906/vet-1201-45; the title indicates a molecular first-detection report with no pathophysiological content.
title: First detection and molecular identification of Babesia gibsoni in two dogs from the Aydin Province of Turkey
rationale: Duplicate of DOI:10.3906/vet-1201-45; title indicates a molecular first-detection report, with no treatment suggested.

original_rationale: Routine case report of first molecular detection in two dogs with no haematology or mechanistic data.
title: First detection and molecular identification of Babesia gibsoni in two dogs from the Aydın Province of Turkey
journal: TURKISH JOURNAL OF VETERINARY AND ANIMAL SCIENCES
rationale: First molecular detection in two dogs; one had pyrexia, weakness and pallor, but no treatment or outcome is described.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract (PubMed): the neurological signs were attributed to confirmed tick-borne encephalitis, not to Babesia. The babesiosis itself is described only as routine diagnosis and treatment, and the report centres on where the infection was acquired (sequencing), so there is no distinct Babesia syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Babesia canis and tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) co-infection in a sled dog.
journal: Annals of agricultural and environmental medicine : AAEM
syndromes: other: clinical signs of babesiosis (not specified)
rationale: Two sled dogs presented with signs of babesiosis and were diagnosed and treated; the first developed neurological signs from concurrent TBE and was alive for serology 3 months later. Weak include: drugs and Babesia-specific outcome are not detailed in the abstract.

original_rationale: Lymphocyte subsets in dogs given culture-derived antigen or a commercial vaccine. The dogs were not infected, so it has no data on host pathophysiology in infected dogs.
title: Quantitative Changes in Selected Lymphocyte Subpopulations after Administration of a Soluble Parasitic Antigen of Babesia Canis to Dogs
journal: Bulletin of the Veterinary Institute in Pulawy
rationale: Lymphocyte subsets after vaccination with a soluble parasite antigen in uninfected dogs.

original_rationale: Based on title and record type. Europe PMC confirms a Letter/Case Report with no abstract. A single imported dog detected in quarantine is a routine diagnostic case with no sign of a distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Babesia vogeli in a quarantined dog.
rationale: Letter/case report of B. vogeli detected in a quarantined imported dog; MeSH terms are diagnostic only, with no therapeutic-use terms, so treatment and outcome are unknown (may be a detection-only report).

original_rationale: Based on the abstract. The antibody responses are used as serological markers of exposure in an acaricide-use and infection-status study, not as host immunopathology. The three clinical babesiosis cases are only counted, with no host data.
title: Effect of owner-controlled acaricidal treatment on tick infestation and immune response to tick-borne pathogens in naturally infested dogs from Eastern Austria.
rationale: Acaricide use and seroresponse study; three clinical cases only counted.

original_rationale: Practice article on vector-borne diseases in UK dogs and cats. Babesiosis is only one of many topics and the article has no pathophysiological focus.
title: Vector-borne diseases and their implications for cats and dogs
rationale: General vector-borne disease practice article; babesiosis only mentioned, no treated dogs.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract. This is a drug-efficacy and resistance study with parasitaemia and relapse endpoints. The ALT increases and hyperphosphatasia are reported as drug side effects, not as disease pathophysiology.
title: The in vitro interactions and in vivo efficacy of atovaquone and proguanil against Babesia gibsoni infection in dogs.
rationale: Experimentally infected dogs treated with Malarone; parasitaemia fell with clinical improvement, then all relapsed with M121I mutation; side effects reported.

original_rationale: Based on abstract: a single case of diagnosing a piroplasm in a puppy with severe regenerative anaemia. The novel points are geographic (first in Scandinavia) and suspected vertical transmission, not a distinct syndrome or a host-side mechanistic observation, so it stays a routine case report.
title: Theileria annae in a young Swedish dog.
rationale: Severe regenerative anaemia in a puppy but no treatment or outcome described; Theileria annae.

original_rationale: Based on title and abstract: clinicopathological findings and treatment in dogs that all had babesiosis plus ehrlichiosis. Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated from the co-infection, and it reads as a routine report of diagnosis and treatment.
title: Clinicopathological Findings and Successful Management of Concurrent Infection of Babesiosis and Ehrlichiosis In Dogs
rationale: Reports clinicopathological findings and successful treatment of concurrent babesiosis and ehrlichiosis in dogs; abstract gives few details.

original_rationale: Field efficacy trial of an imidacloprid/flumethrin collar against ticks and pathogen transmission; no host pathophysiological data.
title: Efficacy of an imidacloprid/flumethrin collar against fleas, ticks and tick-borne pathogens in dogs.
rationale: Collar field trial for tick control and pathogen transmission prevention.

original_rationale: Based on abstract: a cTnT study of canine monocytic ehrlichiosis. Its only Babesia data come from a 7-dog 'Babesia and/or Hepatozoon' group, so Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated.
title: Evaluation of Hematology Profiles and Measurement of Serum Cardiac Troponin Level in Canine Monocytic Ehrlichiosis
journal: The Thai Journal of Veterinary Medicine
rationale: Troponin study in ehrlichiosis; Babesia dogs a pooled comparator group, no treatment.

original_rationale: Based on abstract: a routine single case of a triple infection (diagnosis and treatment). The anaemia, thrombocytopenia and biochemical changes cannot be put down to Babesia, and no distinct syndrome is described.
title: Babesia canis vogeli, Ehrlichia canis, and Anaplasma platys infection in a dog.
rationale: Dog with anaemia, thrombocytopenia and hyperbilirubinaemia co-infected with B. vogeli, E. canis and A. platys; recovered on doxycycline and imidocarb.

original_rationale: Based on the PMC full text (PMC3793166): haematology is given only pooled for all 47 ehrlichiosis dogs, and only one dog had E. canis plus B. gibsoni. No Babesia-specific host data can be separated.
title: Clinical and hematological study of canine Ehrlichiosis with other hemoprotozoan parasites in Kolkata, West Bengal, India
journal: Asian Pacific journal of tropical biomedicine
rationale: Clinical and haematological description of ehrlichiosis with co-infections; no treatment or outcome.

original_rationale: Consensus statement on serology-positive glomerular disease, mainly Borrelia and Leishmania; Babesia is mentioned only in passing with no Babesia-specific data.
title: Consensus Recommendations for Treatment for Dogs with Serology Positive Glomerular Disease
rationale: Glomerular disease consensus; Babesia mentioned only as a seroreactive exposure.

original_rationale: Based on abstract: a vaccine protection trial whose endpoints are vaccine-antigen antibody titres and parasitaemia after challenge, with no mechanistic host-response outcomes. This follows the round 1-3 precedent for vaccine trials (for example PMID:29279083).
title: Prime-boost vaccination with plasmid DNA followed by recombinant vaccinia virus expressing BgGARP induced a partial protective immunity to inhibit Babesia gibsoni proliferation in dogs.
rationale: Vaccine challenge trial with antibody and parasitaemia endpoints.

original_rationale: Abstract: the study is about vertical transmission, shown by identical 18S sequences in three pups and their dam. The pups' disease is not described beyond 'symptoms', and the dam's splenomegaly is used as evidence of infection, so the report has no usable pathophysiological content.
title: The first evidence for vertical transmission of Babesia canis in a litter of Central Asian Shepherd dogs.
journal: Annals of agricultural and environmental medicine : AAEM
rationale: Vertical transmission evidence; symptoms not described and no treatment.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract, these are two routine diagnosis-and-treatment cases with standard signs and blood counts. The fatal case is put down to hepatic damage and anaemia, but no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation is described, so the case-report exclusion applies.
title: Babesiosis in dogs: A report of two different cases
rationale: Two dogs with fever, anaemia and, in one, oliguria, icterus and thrombocytopenia; both treated with diminazene, one recovered and one died of hepatic damage.

original_rationale: IMPDH inhibitors tested on recombinant enzyme, in vitro cultures and a mouse model; drug-target work with no canine host data.
title: Mycophenolic acid, mycophenolate mofetil, mizoribine, ribavirin, and 7-nitroindole inhibit propagation of Babesia parasites by targeting inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase.
species: B. gibsoni, B. bovis, B. microti
rationale: Enzyme, in vitro and mouse study; no infected dogs.

original_rationale: In vitro doxycycline sensitivity of cultured B. gibsoni by real-time PCR; no host data.
title: Evaluation of doxycycline sensitivity in vitro against Babesia gibsoni by Real Time-PCR
journal: Journal of the Bangladesh Agricultural University
rationale: In vitro doxycycline sensitivity only.

original_rationale: From the abstract and MeSH: a Malarone/doxycycline trial in 8 dogs with parasitaemia and relapse endpoints. The anaemia and biochemistry are treatment-response measures, not a host-mechanism focus, which matches how rounds 1-3 handled drug trials.
title: Efficacy of Malarone(®) in dogs naturally infected with Babesia gibsoni.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Eight naturally infected dogs given Malarone with or without doxycycline; parasitaemia and anaemia improved, relapses and retreatment reported.

original_rationale: From the abstract: an acaricide trial on blocking transmission. Hyperthermia in the control dogs served only as an infection endpoint and no host-response data are reported, which matches earlier acaricide-trial exclusions.
title: The ability of an oral formulation of afoxolaner to block the transmission of Babesia canis by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks to dogs.
rationale: Afoxolaner transmission-blocking trial; rescue treatment of controls not the study question.

original_rationale: Prevalence of tick-borne pathogens in dogs in Thailand, with a treatment and parasite-elimination component. It reports no host pathophysiological data.
title: Molecular detection and treatment of tick-borne pathogens in domestic dogs in Khon Kaen, northeastern Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
rationale: Prevalence survey with treatment and parasite clearance but no clinical presentation of the treated dogs.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a drug efficacy and safety study. The BUN/creatinine rise was AmB nephrotoxicity at 1 mg/kg and the methaemoglobin change was drug-induced in normal erythrocytes in vitro, so neither is host pathophysiology of the infection; the rescue is declined.
title: In vitro and in vivo safety and efficacy studies of amphotericin B on Babesia gibsoni.
rationale: Experimentally infected dogs given amphotericin B; parasitaemia fell then recurred and BUN and creatinine rose at 1 mg/kg. Largely in vitro, with limited clinical description.

original_rationale: Based on title and venue only (no abstract available): a conference proceedings item (Korean Society of Veterinary Clinics academic conference proceedings) on the clinical efficacy of atovaquone/proguanil, so it is both a conference abstract and a treatment-efficacy topic.
title: Clinical Efficacy of Atovaquone / Proguanil Hydrochlodie (Malarone ® ) in Dogs Infected with Babesia gibsoni in Jeju
rationale: Korean Society of Veterinary Clinics conference proceedings entry on atovaquone/proguanil in B. gibsoni-infected dogs; conference abstract.

original_rationale: In vitro and mouse growth-inhibition study of trichostatin A; no infected-dog host data.
title: Trichostatin A, a potential drug for treatment of animal Babesia infections
species: B. gibsoni in vitro, B. microti mouse
rationale: In vitro and mouse study.

original_rationale: Based on the title only; the OpenAlex record and KrishiKosh landing page give no abstract or journal. The title describes a routine single-pup clinical case report with no sign of a distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Babesia canis infection in a Labrador pup- A clinical case report
rationale: Single Labrador pup case report held only in the KrishiKosh repository; no abstract or venue, so content and peer-review status are unknown.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract and PMC full text (PMC4261574): none of the 83 dogs had a B. vogeli single infection. The 5 B. vogeli dogs were all co-infected and were pooled into a co-infection group, so Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated out.
title: Evaluation of blood and bone marrow in selected canine vector-borne diseases.
rationale: Bone marrow cytology in vector-borne infections; no treatment.

original_rationale: In vitro drug sensitivity study of artemisinin derivatives; no host data.
title: The efficacy of artemisinin, artemether, and lumefantrine against Babesia gibsoni in vitro.
rationale: In vitro drug study.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a general review of cardiac troponins in dogs. Babesiosis appears only in a list of conditions with raised troponin, so the review's subject is not canine babesiosis; the rescue is declined.
title: Clinical use of cardiac troponins in dogs.
rationale: Troponin review; babesiosis a passing mention.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract. This is a routine single case of Ehrlichia/Babesia co-infection, diagnosed by smear and cured with imidocarb and doxycycline. The haemorrhagic signs and red urine cannot be attributed to Babesia rather than Ehrlichia, and no mechanistic observation or distinct Babesia syndrome is described.
title: Lahore Canine Fever in a Racing Greyhound
journal: Advances in Animal and Veterinary Sciences
rationale: Greyhound with fever, red urine and haemorrhagic signs, Babesia and Ehrlichia co-infection; clinical and parasitological cure after imidocarb and doxycycline.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract. This is a routine single case with the typical presentation (haemolytic anaemia, haemoglobinaemia, leukocytosis) and treatment. It describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, and its focus is on occurrence and zoonotic advice.
title: A CASE OF DIPYLIDIASIS AND BABESIOSIS IN A 2-YEAR OLD MONGREL (BITCH) -
rationale: Bitch with B. canis and Dipylidium caninum, haemolytic anaemia, haemoglobinaemia and leukocytosis, treated parenterally and orally according to signs; the abstract gives no outcome, so the outcome criterion is unconfirmed.

original_rationale: Archaeological and historical argument about disease constraining dog spread in Africa; canine babesiosis is discussed as a threat without host pathophysiological data.
title: Did disease constrain the spread of domestic dogs (Canis familiaris) into Sub-Saharan Africa?
rationale: Archaeological and historical argument, no dog clinical data.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract summary from Semantic Scholar (the AJOL page returned no content): a household prevalence survey (9/101 infected) with risk factors such as age, sex, breed, management and ticks. No host haematology or pathophysiology is reported.
title: Infection of dogs with <i>Babesia canis</i> in Gwagwalada metropolis of Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, Nigeria
rationale: Prevalence survey; no abstract, no treatment described.

original_rationale: Case report of idiopathic IMHA in a dog that tested negative for Babesia; the dog is not Babesia-infected, so there are no eligible host data.
title: Triple Immunosuppressive Therapy of Immune-mediated Hemolytic Anemia in a Dog: Case-report
journal: Bulletin of University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca Veterinary Medicine
rationale: Idiopathic IMHA, dog tested negative for Babesia.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a fluralaner prevention trial whose endpoints are tick efficacy and infection prevention. Rectal temperature and clinical signs were monitored only to detect infection, and infected controls were rescue-treated with no host pathophysiological results reported. This matches earlier rounds, which excluded acaricide prevention trials.
title: Prevention of transmission of Babesia canis by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks to dogs treated orally with fluralaner chewable tablets (Bravecto™).
rationale: Fluralaner transmission prevention trial.

original_rationale: Canine distemper outbreak report in which a few dogs had vector-borne infections including Babesia; no Babesia-specific host data can be separated out.
title: Clinical and molecular investigation of a canine distemper outbreak and vector-borne infections in a group of rescue dogs imported from Hungary to Switzerland.
rationale: Distemper outbreak; Babesia found in a few dogs, not treated or discussed separately.

original_rationale: Two-case report of the first molecular identification of B. gibsoni in Slovakia; the abstract describes diagnosis and treatment with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: First molecular identification of Babesia gibsoni in dogs from Slovakia, central Europe.
rationale: Two molecular identification cases; abstract gives no clinical course or treatment.

original_rationale: This is a conference proceedings entry (Korean Society of Veterinary Clinics) with no abstract. The title describes a treatment efficacy comparison, which would be excluded in any case.
title: Clinical Efficacy of Atovaquone/Proguanil and Azithromycin Combination Therapy in Dogs Naturally Infected with Babesia gibsoni
rationale: Korean Society of Veterinary Clinics conference proceedings entry on atovaquone/proguanil plus azithromycin in naturally infected dogs; conference abstract.

original_rationale: Allele-specific PCR for the atovaquone-resistance cytochrome b variant in parasite DNA from infected dogs. It reports parasite genetics only, with no host data.
title: The epidemiological survey for atovaquone resistant related gene of Babesia gibsoni in Japan.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Resistance genotyping of parasite DNA; no treated dogs described.

original_rationale: From Crossref metadata (no abstract reachable; the Elsevier landing page did not load): a single-page item, J Comp Pathol 154(1):73, January 2016. That position matches the ESVP/ECVP annual meeting abstracts printed in that issue, so this is a conference abstract and not a full paper.
title: Comparison of the Pathological, Histological, Cytological and Genotyping Results Between Imidocarb-Dipropionate Treated and Untreated Dogs Infected with Babesia canis
rationale: Single-page item in J Comp Pathol 154(1):73 matching the ESVP/ECVP meeting abstracts; conference abstract.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a routine single case of diagnosis, doxycycline treatment and transfusion for severe anaemia. The anaemia is the usual presentation, with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
title: Clinical Management of Babesiosis in a Dog along with Blood Transfusion
rationale: Doberman with severe anaemia (PCV 10%) given doxycycline and transfusion; haematology improved and dog recovered.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a routine single case of triple co-infection with diagnosis and treatment. Its cytopenias cannot be attributed to Babesia, so the mixed-infection rule is not met, and it describes no distinct syndrome.
title: Ocorrência de infecção concomitante natural por Ehrlichia sp., Anaplasma sp. E Babesia sp. em cão assistido no hospital veterinário da universidade federal de Uberlândia
journal: Revista Científica Eletrônica de Medicina Veterinária
rationale: Dog with thrombocytopenia and Ehrlichia, Anaplasma and Babesia co-infection treated with doxycycline and imidocarb; normal counts and no parasites at recheck.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a general narrative review of point-of-care lactate in small animals. Babesiosis is named once among conditions with raised lactate, so canine babesiosis pathophysiology is not the subject and the review adds no babesia-specific content.
title: Point of Care Measurement of Lactate.
rationale: Lactate review; babesiosis a passing mention.

original_rationale: Based on PubMed, Europe PMC and Crossref metadata (Wiley page 403; the repository PDF is a different paper): a single-page JSAP case item with no abstract and MeSH major topic 'diagnosis'. It reads as a routine autochthonous diagnosis with no sign of a distinct syndrome or mechanism.
title: Autochthonous babesiosis in the United Kingdom.
journal: The Journal of small animal practice
rationale: Short JSAP case item on autochthonous UK babesiosis; no abstract, MeSH major topic diagnosis and no therapeutic-use terms, so treatment and outcome are unknown.

original_rationale: Title concerns the availability of treatments for canine babesiosis, and no abstract is given. The topic is treatment access (likely a letter), not host pathophysiology.
title: Availability of treatments for babesiosis in dogs
rationale: Title indicates a letter on drug availability, with no treated dogs or presentation described.

original_rationale: Fluralaner prevention of tick transmission of B. canis, with infection status as the endpoint. No host pathophysiological outcomes.
title: Prevention of transmission of Babesia canis by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks to dogs after topical administration of fluralaner spot-on solution.
rationale: Fluralaner tick-transmission prevention trial in uninfected dogs; endpoint is infection prevented, with no clinical disease treated.

original_rationale: Based on the abstract: a single B. gibsoni case with routine findings (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, fever, splenomegaly) and a report of response to a drug combination. It describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, so the routine case report rule applies.
title: New Therapeutic Protocol for Canine Babesiosis: A Case Report
journal: Journal of Dairy Veterinary & Animal Research
rationale: One dog with fever, anaemia, thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly treated with a 10-day drug combination; improved from day 4 and recovered.

original_rationale: Based on the one-page English abstract in the publisher PDF: a treatment study of transfusing cryopreserved packed red cells after Piro-Stop. The only endpoints are percentage rises in Hb, Hct and RBC count against untransfused dogs, with no mechanistic or pathophysiological outcomes.
title: Application of Cryopreserved Packed Red Blood Cells to Treat Anaemic Syndrome in Canine Babesiosis
rationale: One-page item listed in the journal issue's Abstracts section (p.186): a short abstract on cryopreserved red-cell transfusion for anaemia in babesiosis, not a full peer-reviewed paper.

original_rationale: Duplicate record of DOI:10.15407/cryo26.02.186 (Russian-language title, same journal page 186). It is a treatment study of red-cell transfusion with only Hb, Hct and RBC response endpoints, so the decision is the same.
title: Применение криоконсервированной эритроцитарной массы при коррекции анемического синдрома у собак, вызванного Babesia canis
rationale: Russian-language duplicate of DOI:10.15407/cryo26.02.186, a one-page abstract in the journal's Abstracts section; same decision.

original_rationale: Title only: no abstract could be found, and the Springer page is behind a sign-in redirect. The title describes clinical management of a single dog with a triple infection including leptospirosis. Findings in such a case cannot be attributed to Babesia, and the title points to a routine management report rather than a distinct syndrome.
title: Clinical management of a Labrador retriever dog concurrently infected with Leptospira interrogans, Babesia gibsoni and Dirofilaria repens
rationale: Six-page report of clinical management of one dog with Leptospira, B. gibsoni and Dirofilaria repens; title implies treatment, but presentation and outcome cannot be confirmed without the abstract.

original_rationale: Review of the diagnostic protocol and of therapy by species, with no host pathophysiology.
title: Actualizarea protocolului de diagnostic în babesioza canină
rationale: Review of the diagnostic protocol that also covers therapy management and drug response by Babesia species. Treatment is part of the subject, though the emphasis is on diagnosis.

original_rationale: Practical overview of several tick-borne diseases for veterinary nurses. It is not a pathophysiology review of canine babesiosis.
title: Tick-borne diseases in dogs
rationale: Narrative nursing review updating babesiosis and other canine tick-borne diseases, including limitations of diagnosis and treatment; included as a review whose subject includes treatment of canine babesiosis, though detail was not verified.

original_rationale: Primarily a treatment-efficacy study (imidocarb dipropionate and/or alpha-lipoic acid in experimental B. vogeli infection). Accessible information shows only clinical signs and haematology (PCV, RBC, Hb) as endpoints, with no mechanistic or pathophysiological outcomes. Borderline: an infected-untreated arm and an antioxidant arm exist, but full text is paywalled and was not read.
title: Ameliorative effects of alpha-lipoic acid and imidocarb dipropionate on clinico-haematological changes induced by experimental Babesia canis vogeli infection in dogs
rationale: 17-page study of dogs experimentally infected with B. canis vogeli and treated with imidocarb and/or alpha-lipoic acid, with clinical signs and haematology (PCV, RBC, Hb) as endpoints per the earlier screen's accessible information.

original_rationale: Bibliographic record exists (Crossref), but no abstract or full text is accessible (eLIBRARY.ru blocked, doi.org redirects to it), so eligibility cannot be judged. Title indicates a plasmapheresis treatment study; pathophysiological content, species and design cannot be confirmed. No note written.
title: Effectiveness of using plasmapheresis in polyorganic intoxications after infection of dogs with Babesia
rationale: Title indicates plasmapheresis for multi-organ intoxication in Babesia-infected dogs (Veterinariya 23(7):37-41); no abstract to confirm design or outcomes.

original_rationale: No abstract or full text could be accessed and the record is confirmed only by OpenAlex (journal, volume 15(2), pages 36-39). No DOI or PMID; the CABI landing page returned HTTP 410 and the CABI digital library returned 403; Crossref returned no match; web search did not find the article. Without an abstract or full text, eligibility (mechanistic or syndromic content versus a therapy-focused case report) cannot be judged, and the record cannot be authoritatively verified.
title: Therapeutic management of hepatic failure and ascites in a Babesia gibsoni infected Labrador retriever dog.
journal: Journal of Indian Veterinary Association, Kerala
rationale: Title indicates therapeutic management of hepatic failure and ascites in one B. gibsoni-infected Labrador, probably qualifying, but no abstract or full text is reachable.

original_rationale: Treatment-efficacy study (prednisolone vs prednisolone plus azathioprine) in 13 dogs with B. gibsoni-associated secondary IMHA, uncontrolled and with concurrent antiprotozoal therapy. Babesia-specific data are limited to day-0 and post-treatment means in a mixed haemolytic-anaemia enrolment (only flow-cytometry IMHA-positive dogs entered, so no prevalence or severity inference); pathophysiological content is incidental. Borderline: day-0 haemogram, platelets and chemistry exist for the B. gibsoni subgroup (Hb about 3.3-4.3 g/dL; platelets about 50,000-71,000/uL), but the species-level identification method is not described and the percentages in the abstract are internally inconsistent.
title: Treatment of Secondary Immune Mediated Hemolytic Anaemia of Dogs in Chennai, Tamil Nadu
rationale: Secondary IMHA dogs, 13 of them with B. gibsoni, treated with prednisolone with or without azathioprine plus specific therapy. Hb, PCV, platelets and clinical improvement to day 28 are reported, but the Babesia subgroup is mixed with other causes.

original_rationale: Single-dog case report whose focus is hemodialysis efficacy for AKI, not babesiosis pathophysiology. The link to babesiosis is asserted but not documented in the paper: no Babesia species, no diagnostic method, no parasitaemia, no pre-referral data. Pathophysiological content is generic literature discussion; the only case data are serial creatinine/urea/phosphorus under dialysis plus nonspecific anaemia and thrombocytopenia. Timeline is internally inconsistent (Methods: AKI grade IV diagnosed before referral; Results/Discussion: deterioration within 24-48 h after imidocarb, a drug-related confounder). Borderline: authors frame it as AKI secondary to babesiosis, so a reviewer wanting renal-complication case reports could reconsider.
title: Acute kidney injury in a dog successfully treated with hemodialysis: a case report
rationale: One dog with AKI after treated babesiosis, managed with haemodialysis and recovering renal function. The Babesia link is asserted but not documented in detail.

original_rationale: Screening marked the record uncertain. The abstract reports a treatment comparison (oral homeopathic Crotalus horridus 200C in 13 dogs versus diminazene in 20 dogs) with clinical scores and parasitaemia as outcomes, and says haematological values showed no change without giving values. The full text was not read (no PMC or Europe PMC copy; not open access per Europe PMC), so baseline haematology of the infected dogs could not be confirmed and the record falls under the guide's treatment-study-only exclusion.
title: Clinical management of babesiosis in dogs with homeopathic Crotalus horridus 200C.
journal: Homeopathy: the journal of the Faculty of Homeopathy
rationale: Comparison of homeopathic Crotalus horridus (13 dogs) with diminazene (20 dogs) in B. gibsoni dogs with listed clinical signs. Clinical scores and parasitaemia improved in both groups.

original_rationale: Crossref and OpenAlex confirm the record exists as an 11-page article (Pol J Nat Sci 23(1):257-267, 2008), but no abstract or full text could be reached (packet, data/markdown, Crossref and OpenAlex all have none; the metapress link is defunct). The title alone does not show whether the case report describes a distinct syndrome or mechanism rather than routine treatment, so eligibility cannot be judged.
title: Peritoneal Dialysis in A Dog with Acute Renal Failure Caused by the Infection with Babesia Canis
rationale: Title describes peritoneal dialysis for acute renal failure in a B. canis-infected dog, likely an include, but the outcome cannot be confirmed.

original_rationale: The full text (3-page case report) describes a dog with smear-suspected B. canis whose neurological signs were attributed to rabies, confirmed by FAT and PCR on brain tissue after euthanasia. It reports no necropsy or histopathology findings that separate Babesia-specific cerebral or organ findings from rabies, so it is a routine single co-infection case of diagnosis and treatment.
title: Dual infection of rabies virus and Babesia canis in a dog: a case report
rationale: One dog with icterus, weakness and suspected cerebral babesiosis that did not respond to treatment and was found post mortem to have rabies. Treatment drugs are not named in the abstract, so this is borderline.

original_rationale: The record is a treatment trial comparing clindamycin, diminazene and imidocarb with atovaquone and azithromycin in naturally infected dogs. Its reported endpoints are recovery, relapse, therapy duration and parasite CYTb M121I mutation (parasite-side), so it falls under treatment_efficacy. The abstract says haematological parameters were recorded but gives no values, and the full text could not be reached (publisher page returned 403), so no host pathophysiological data could be confirmed.
title: The therapeutic efficacy of two antibabesial strategies against Babesia gibsoni.
rationale: Naturally infected dogs treated with atovaquone plus azithromycin (17) or clindamycin, diminazene and imidocarb (13). Recovery, relapse and therapy duration are reported, and haematology was recorded.

original_rationale: The record exists as a published 2-page item (Comp Clin Pathol 2015;24(5):1221-1222, confirmed by Crossref and OpenAlex), but no abstract or full text could be reached. Whether it reports a distinct syndrome or a mechanistic observation, rather than a routine diagnosis-and-treatment case, cannot be judged from the title alone.
title: Cutaneous lesions due to babesiosis in a dog
rationale: Two-page report of cutaneous lesions due to babesiosis in one dog; treatment and outcome cannot be confirmed without the abstract.
